# PR #172 correctness verdict

**PASS** at `ec31a8c1e76c44201d5e8ebd9676788aabaa8d24`. The one-line community-route addition is accurate and covered by the existing route-command test. No findings.

`skills/pij/references/routes/community.md:66` describes delivered as ending the work identified by its PR, not sweeping historical PR holdings. It correctly recommends a one-time explicit batch release for the old backlog. `pij directory release --batch '<file>' --why '<reason>'` uses the supported flags, quotes both values, and specifies the existing one-role/instance-and-seat-per-line format and single directory commit. It does not instruct a blind release of every current holding.

The route is **92 lines**, below 100. The structural gate explicitly checks that file against a 100-line budget (`harness/scripts/pij-skill-check.sh:71`).

The Rust test reads the actual community route (`crates/cli/tests/skill_verb_coverage.rs:393`), extracts inline backtick commands as well as fenced commands (`:153`), and checks their native leaf flags/required usage (`:322,429`). The author reports the restored negative control: removing `--why` from this new line fails `the_community_route_and_templates_print_real_commands` with `pij directory release --batch '<file>': a required flag is missing`. This demonstrates coverage of the addition, not merely generic verb-table coverage.

CI run `42434204381` associated with this exact head passed. Its JUnit artifact confirms the route-command test executed and passed; the suite records 2,194 passing Rust cases with zero failures/errors. Node 22/24 and Rust lint/test checks passed, as did Delivers. `pr-freeze` reported FINAL: matching heads, CLEAN, ready and successful latest checks. `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.

No local builds/tests, product edits, credentials, live-daemon probes, merge or push. The detached worktree remains clean at the requested SHA. This PR changes one documentation line and adds no runtime loop, timer or launch.
